# 0066: A harness says which commands a shell call ran

Status: accepted, 2026-10-08.
Refines [0048](0048-coverage-reads-the-command-the-shell-ran.md) (shell variables are expanded) with where the commands come from.

## Context

Codex's `exec` tool takes a JavaScript script, not a shell command.
Each command sits inside it as `tools.exec_command({cmd: "...", workdir: "..."})`.
Skill coverage read the whole script as one shell line.

The usual command opens with `skill_root='<dir>'`, then runs `bun run "$skill_root/scripts/gate.ts"`.
Read whole, the script's first statement swallowed the assignment, so the variable never expanded.
Seven codex sessions that ran the skill's gates recorded no script run at all.

## Decision

**A harness says which commands one shell call ran.** `Harness.shell_commands` takes a call's input and returns each command with its working directory.
The base reads a `command` or `cmd` key, as coverage did before.

**Codex unwraps its scripts.** It reads the object literal after each `exec_command(`, with keys bare or quoted and values JSON.
An input it cannot read stays the script text, which is what was matched before.

**The vocabulary carries it.** `Shells` gains `commands`, filled from the harness like `tools` and `persistent`.
Coverage resolves each command on its own, so a variable set in one is expanded within it (ADR 0048).

## Consequences

Replayed against the cache, the seven codex sessions now record the scripts they ran.
The one codex session still recording none ran no script.

A new CLI whose shell tool wraps its commands overrides one method; nothing in `derive/` learns its dialect.

## Lens

Coverage can only attribute a command it can read as a command.
How a CLI wraps its commands is that CLI's business, so the harness unwraps them.
